summary: LLM Doctor is the loop's model-backend qualifier: a 7-step diagnosis that runs config sanity (Step 0), detects the Backend (sglang/vllm/ollama/llama.cpp/lmstudio), lists ModelInfo and checks max_model_len against MIN_RECOMMENDED_CONTEXT, validates the chat template, runs a connectivity/latency test measuring tokens_per_second and tool_calling_works, then probes a capability matrix (tool calling, SSE streaming, chat_template_kwargs thinking, multimodal). Every probe is a DoctorCheckResult (Pass/Warn/Fail/Skip) with a fix_hint, rolled into a DoctorReport with had_failures. It confirms the reason engine can actually do what the loop assumes before the first LLM call.
context_basis: recommendations were formed with src/llm_doctor.rs read in the context of the full engine (~600k budget framing), where the reason stage depends on tool-calling, streaming, thinking, and adequate context; llm_doctor qualifies those capabilities before the loop trusts them.

examples.title: Qualify the reason backend before the loop runs
examples.intent: Confirm the LLM endpoint can serve the loop's reasoning needs before spending budget.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: run_llm_doctor builds a DoctorReport whose had_failures flag gates the loop: a Fail on a capability the reason stage depends on stops the loop before its first LLM call.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tapping the llm_doctor node runs the full 7-step diagnosis and stamps the reason gate.
touch_interaction.visual: A capability matrix badge fills; the reason gate glows green only when had_failures is false.

examples.mini_scenario: Diagnosis passes tool-calling and streaming but fails thinking; the loop starts with thinking-control disabled.
examples.pitfall: had_failures reflects Fail outcomes only; a Warn (e.g. no tool_calls produced) doesn't block but still degrades the loop.

examples.title: Detect the backend from the endpoint
examples.intent: Identify whether the endpoint is vLLM, SGLang, Ollama, llama.cpp, or LM Studio.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: detect_backend inspects headers and the models body to resolve a Backend enum, so later steps and the loop tune capability expectations to that server's known behavior.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-pressing the backend chip shows the detected server and its detection evidence.
touch_interaction.visual: A server icon morphs to the detected backend's logo; Unknown shows a question-mark badge with the hint.

examples.mini_scenario: Detection reads vLLM headers and reports Backend::Vllm, so the loop expects native SSE streaming.
examples.pitfall: Backend::Unknown(hint) still runs the probes; don't skip capability testing just because detection was ambiguous.

examples.title: List available models on the endpoint
examples.intent: Confirm the configured model is actually served.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: Step 2 populates available_models and a model_available DoctorCheckResult, so the loop fails fast if it's pointed at a model the backend doesn't host.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Spreading the model chip fans out every model ID the endpoint lists.
touch_interaction.visual: The configured model highlights green if present, red if absent among the listed IDs.

examples.mini_scenario: The config names 'Qwen3.5-122B' and it appears in available_models, so model_available passes.
examples.pitfall: A model present under a slightly different ID still fails the exact match; verify the exact served id string.

examples.title: Check context length against the recommended floor
examples.intent: Ensure the model's context is big enough for the loop's working set.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: Step 2 compares max_model_len and the configured context_length to MIN_RECOMMENDED_CONTEXT (32768), warning when the loop's context budget outruns the model's window.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Pinching the context gauge compares configured vs backend max_model_len.
touch_interaction.visual: A bar shows the configured window against the backend max; amber if below the 32k floor or above the max.

examples.mini_scenario: Backend max_model_len is 8192 but config asks for 32k; a Warn fires so the loop clamps its context budget.
examples.pitfall: Configured context above backend max_model_len silently truncates at runtime; the loop must respect the backend ceiling.

examples.title: Validate the chat template
examples.intent: Confirm the backend applies a usable chat format.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: Step 3 checks the chat template so the reason stage's messages are formatted correctly; a broken template would corrupt every prompt the loop sends.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Double-tapping the template chip shows the detected chat format.
touch_interaction.visual: A green check for a recognized template; amber when the format can't be confirmed.

examples.mini_scenario: The Qwen chat template is detected, so the loop trusts role formatting for its multi-turn prompts.
examples.pitfall: A missing template can make a backend silently concatenate roles; verify format before trusting multi-turn behavior.

examples.title: Run a connectivity and latency test
examples.intent: Measure round-trip latency before the loop depends on the endpoint.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: Step 5's ConnectionTestResult records latency and feeds latency_ms into the report, giving control a per-call cost estimate for its iteration budget.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tapping the latency chip fires a test request and shows the round trip.
touch_interaction.visual: A stopwatch fills; green for fast, amber for slow, with the millisecond figure.

examples.mini_scenario: The connection test returns 480ms latency, which control uses to estimate total time for a 12-iteration loop.
examples.pitfall: The connection test has a 30-45s timeout; a cold-loading model can look 'slow' on the first probe but be fast after.

examples.title: Estimate tokens per second
examples.intent: Know the generation speed the loop can expect.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: extract_tokens_per_second derives tokens_per_second from the test response, letting control predict how long generation-heavy iterations will take.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Pinching the throughput gauge expands to a tokens/sec readout.
touch_interaction.visual: A speedometer needle settles on the measured rate; low rates tint amber.

examples.mini_scenario: The probe reports 38 tok/s, so control estimates a 4k-token response will take ~2 minutes.
examples.pitfall: Throughput is Optional; if the response lacks usage timing it's None, and the loop must not assume a rate.

examples.title: Probe whether tool calling actually works
examples.intent: Confirm the backend emits real tool_calls, not just claims support.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: Step 5 sets tool_calling_works by checking whether a probe request produced tool_calls; the loop's act stage only trusts tool-based flows when this is true.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-pressing the tool-calling chip runs a forced tool-call probe.
touch_interaction.visual: A wrench icon lights green on tool_calls produced, amber on 'did not produce tool_calls'.

examples.mini_scenario: The probe forces a function call and the model returns tool_calls, so the loop enables its tool-execution path.
examples.pitfall: tool_calling_works is Option<bool>; None (probe skipped/unreachable) is not the same as false and shouldn't disable tools outright.

examples.title: Probe SSE streaming support
examples.intent: Confirm the loop can stream tokens for responsive output.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: probe_capabilities sets streaming from whether an SSE request returned chunks; the loop enables incremental UI/verify only when streaming actually responds.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Flicking the streaming chip fires an SSE probe and watches for chunks.
touch_interaction.visual: Token chunks stream across the chip as dots when SSE responds; a flat line when it doesn't.

examples.mini_scenario: The probe gets SSE chunks so the loop streams responses; the fix_hint warns to disable proxy buffering if not.
examples.pitfall: A reverse proxy buffering SSE can make streaming falsely appear broken; the fix_hint flags this exact cause.

examples.title: Probe chat_template_kwargs thinking support
examples.intent: Confirm the backend accepts Qwen-style thinking toggles.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: The thinking probe checks whether the backend honors chat_template_kwargs; if not, the loop's reason stage cannot control the thinking budget and must opt out.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Double-tapping the thinking chip toggles a probe with enable_thinking on/off.
touch_interaction.visual: A brain icon glows when kwargs are accepted; greys out when ignored.

examples.mini_scenario: SGLang accepts chat_template_kwargs, so the loop can disable thinking on cheap steps to save tokens.
examples.pitfall: A backend that ignores the kwarg looks like it accepted it; the fix_hint recommends explicit opt-out via extra_body.

examples.title: Heuristically flag a multimodal model
examples.intent: Guess whether the model can handle vision input.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: looks_multimodal inspects the model name to set Capabilities.multimodal, so the loop only wires image inputs into reason when the model plausibly supports them.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tapping the multimodal chip shows whether the name heuristic matched.
touch_interaction.visual: An eye icon opens green for likely-vision, greyed for text-only.

examples.mini_scenario: A model named '...-VL' matches the heuristic, so the loop offers screenshot inputs to the reason stage.
examples.pitfall: This is a name heuristic, not a live probe; a mislabeled model can falsely enable (or hide) real vision support.

examples.title: Render the unified capability matrix
examples.intent: Present tools/streaming/thinking/multimodal as one PASS/WARN/FAIL grid.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: Step 7 pushes each probe into report.capabilities as a DoctorCheckResult, giving the loop one matrix to decide which reason/act features to enable.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Spreading the matrix node expands the four capability rows.
touch_interaction.visual: A 4-row grid: each row green/amber/red with its detail and fix hint on tap.

examples.mini_scenario: The matrix shows tools PASS, streaming PASS, thinking WARN, multimodal SKIP, guiding the loop's feature flags.
examples.pitfall: Each row is independent; a PASS on streaming says nothing about tool calling, so read the whole matrix, not one cell.

examples.title: Skip probes when the endpoint is unreachable
examples.intent: Avoid meaningless probe failures when the endpoint is down.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: When Step 1 reachability fails, downstream capability checks yield CheckOutcome::Skip rather than Fail, so the loop distinguishes 'unreachable' from 'unsupported'.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tapping a skipped chip explains it was skipped because the endpoint was unreachable.
touch_interaction.visual: Skipped chips render greyed with a dashed border rather than red.

examples.mini_scenario: The endpoint is down; streaming/tools/thinking all show Skip, telling the loop to fix connectivity first.
examples.pitfall: Skip is not Fail; treating skipped capabilities as failures blames the model for what is really a network problem.

examples.title: Reuse config checks as Step 0
examples.intent: Catch config errors before any network probe.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: Step 0 runs doctor::config_checks and maps CheckStatus to CheckOutcome, so a bad endpoint or missing key fails cheaply before the loop attempts a live call.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Drawing an edge from the doctor config node into Step 0 seeds the diagnosis.
touch_interaction.visual: Config sub-chips populate the Step 0 lane before the network steps light up.

examples.mini_scenario: Step 0 flags a missing api_key on a remote endpoint, so llm_doctor never wastes a request that would 401.
examples.pitfall: The Ok->Pass/Warning->Warn/Missing->Fail mapping must stay faithful, or a Missing config would mislabel as a mere Warn.

examples.title: Emit a machine-readable report for CI
examples.intent: Let CI and programmatic callers gate on the diagnosis without parsing text.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: DoctorReport is Serialize, so JSON mode exposes every probe outcome, letting an automated loop-launcher decide go/no-go from structured fields.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Flicking the report node toward the CI lane exports it as JSON.
touch_interaction.visual: The matrix collapses into a JSON document card with had_failures highlighted.

examples.mini_scenario: CI reads report.had_failures=true and refuses to launch the loop against an unqualified backend.
examples.pitfall: Consume the structured fields, not the pretty-printed matrix; scraping human output breaks on formatting changes.

examples.title: Merge extra_body into the probe request
examples.intent: Probe with the same request shape the loop will actually use.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: Probes use merge_extra_body so chat_template_kwargs and other extra params match production, making the capability verdict trustworthy for the real loop.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-pressing the probe chip shows the exact request body including merged extra_body.
touch_interaction.visual: The chip flips to reveal the JSON payload with extra_body fields highlighted.

examples.mini_scenario: The thinking probe merges enable_thinking=false so its result reflects how the loop will actually call the model.
examples.pitfall: Probing without the loop's extra_body can pass a capability the real requests then trip on, giving false confidence.

examples.title: Build a recommendations tree on failure
examples.intent: Turn probe failures into concrete backend fixes.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: Step 6 assembles remediation recommendations (fix_hints per capability), so a Degraded loop can hand the operator or agent a prioritized fix list.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Spreading the recommendations node expands the fix tree by capability.
touch_interaction.visual: A branching tree; each leaf is a fix_hint card tied to its failing capability.

examples.mini_scenario: Thinking WARN yields a hint to use vLLM/SGLang with a Qwen template, guiding the operator's next move.
examples.pitfall: Recommendations are backend-specific; applying a vLLM hint to Ollama can make things worse, so match the detected Backend.

examples.title: Warn when tool_calls aren't produced
examples.intent: Let the loop fall back to text parsing when native tool-calls are absent.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: A tool-calling Warn ('model did not produce tool_calls') tells the loop to route the act stage through text-based tool extraction instead of assuming native calls.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Double-tapping the amber tool chip shows the fallback strategy.
touch_interaction.visual: The wrench icon shows amber with a 'text-fallback' sub-tag.

examples.mini_scenario: The model returns text but no tool_calls; the loop switches to parsing tool intents from the text body.
examples.pitfall: Warn is not Fail; hard-disabling tools on a Warn throws away a workable text-based tool path.

examples.title: Bound every probe with a timeout
examples.intent: Keep the diagnosis from hanging on a stuck endpoint.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: HTTP_TIMEOUT (10s) bounds each probe and the connection test has its own 30-45s window, so a wedged backend degrades to Skip/Fail instead of freezing loop startup.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Rotating the timeout dial adjusts the probe patience within its bounds.
touch_interaction.visual: A countdown ring on each in-flight probe; a timed-out probe snaps to a dashed Skip/Fail state.

examples.mini_scenario: A hung endpoint times out each probe at 10s, so the whole diagnosis returns in seconds with Skip results.
examples.pitfall: Connection-test timeouts are longer than probe timeouts; a cold model needs the longer window, don't clamp it too tight.

examples.title: Gate loop features on the final verdict
examples.intent: Translate the matrix into which loop features are on.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: The loop reads the completed DoctorReport and enables tool-execution, streaming output, thinking control, and vision input only where the matching capability passed, shaping every downstream stage's options.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Pinching the matrix into the loop node applies the capabilities as feature flags.
touch_interaction.visual: Passed capabilities light their corresponding loop-stage nodes; failed ones leave those nodes dim.

examples.mini_scenario: Tools PASS and streaming PASS light the act and output nodes; thinking WARN leaves thinking-control off.
examples.pitfall: Enable per-capability, not all-or-nothing; disabling every feature because one capability failed cripples an otherwise-usable loop.
